# Tabbing to a button shows no keyboard focus indicator

## Context

Ada observed that the checkout example’s Check order button receives keyboard focus without a visible cue. I reproduced it independently at the current `dev` Button source in the real Chromium component fixture.

## The Problem

Mount a `Neo.button.Base` control and Tab into it. In classic Light, classic Dark, Neo Light, Neo Dark and Cyberpunk, the button is the active element and matches `:focus-visible`, but its computed outline and shadow styles are both `none`.

## The Architectural Reality

[Button Base CSS](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7ab5c8466989ef25ad00cf19d484fb9a1244ac43/resources/css/src/button/Base.css#L156) owns the common `:focus` rule. All five bundled themes set its `--button-outline-active` to `none`. The Theme Switcher already shows an explicit keyboard outline. Standard buttons also appear inside clipped controls and on filled backgrounds.

Design authority: [WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html) specifies a mode where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.

## The Fix

Add the shared keyboard outline to Button Base CSS, with an inset contrast band so it remains visible on filled buttons and in clipped layouts. Reuse the semantic focus and neutral surface colors, with system colors for classic themes. Existing pointer styles and disabled semantics stay intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A real Tab onto the Button paints a visible indicator in all five bundled themes.
- [ ] Verify a plain button, a filled or pressed button, and a button inside a clipped control. Pointer focus keeps the existing default treatment and disabled buttons remain skipped by Tab.
- [ ] Extend the Button component regression for the keyboard outline and record the painted before/after result.

## Out of Scope

Changing keyboard order, recoloring the themes, and redesigning the checkout example.
